SECTION 2640 REIMBURSEMENT OF SEPARATE PROPERTY CONTRIBUTIONS — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Alex Lee · Morgan Casey Lee

DECLARATION OF PARTIES AND PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This Family Code Section 2640 Reimbursement Information Sheet concerns Jordan Alex Lee and Morgan Casey Lee, whose marital dissolution or legal separation proceeding is pending, or may be filed, in the California superior court for Sacramento County. It describes what California Family Code section 2640 says about a right, applied at the time the community estate is divided, to reimbursement for separate-property funds a party traces to the acquisition of property of the community estate — for example, a down payment on a residence acquired during the marriage. This information sheet states what the Family Code says about this reimbursement right in general terms. It does not determine, calculate, or assert that the right applies to Jordan Alex Lee and Morgan Casey Lee's specific property or contributions, whether any contribution has been adequately traced to a separate property source, or whether any waiver has occurred; those are matters for the court to decide based on the specific facts, or for Jordan Alex Lee and Morgan Casey Lee to resolve by their own written agreement.

WHAT COUNTS AS A "CONTRIBUTION TO THE ACQUISITION OF PROPERTY" UNDER SECTION 2640
Family Code section 2640 defines "contributions to the acquisition of property," as the term is used in that section, to include down payments, payments for improvements, and payments that reduce the principal of a loan used to finance the purchase or improvement of the property. The statute's definition expressly excludes two categories of payment: payments of interest on the loan, and payments made for maintenance, insurance, or taxation of the property. Only a payment falling within the statute's own included categories is a "contribution to the acquisition of property" for purposes of the reimbursement right described in this document's companion clauses.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "“Contributions to the acquisition of property,” as used in this section, include downpayments, payments for improvements, and payments that reduce the principal of a loan used to finance the purchase or improvement of the property but do not include payments of interest on the loan or payments made for maintenance, insurance, or taxation of the property."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2640(a) (California Legislative Information text), the statute's own definition of "contributions to the acquisition of property," including its express exclusions (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2640.)
  Known gap: This is the actual text of Family Code section 2640(a), the Legislature's own definitional subdivision, fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and confirmed byte-identical across two fetches made with different User-Agent strings. This citation is to the same statutory section, 2640, cited by this document's other authority clauses (which quote subdivisions (b) and (c)) — they are not independent of one another; all are different subdivisions of one enacted section. This document does not address how a court or party establishes that a particular payment falls within one category rather than another (for example, distinguishing a payment that reduces loan principal from a blended payment that also includes interest), which the statute's text does not itself resolve.

THE RIGHT TO REIMBURSEMENT AND THE WRITTEN-WAIVER REQUIREMENT
Family Code section 2640 provides that, in the division of the community estate, a party shall be reimbursed for that party's contributions to the acquisition of property of the community property estate to the extent the party traces the contributions to a separate property source. This right does not apply where the party has made a written waiver of the right to reimbursement, or has signed a writing that has the effect of a waiver. Subject to that written-waiver exception, the statute states the reimbursement right in mandatory terms — the reimbursed party "shall be reimbursed" once separate-source contributions to the community acquisition are traced.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "In the division of the community estate under this division, unless a party has made a written waiver of the right to reimbursement or has signed a writing that has the effect of a waiver, the party shall be reimbursed for the party’s contributions to the acquisition of property of the community property estate to the extent the party traces the contributions to a separate property source."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2640(b) (California Legislative Information text), the reimbursement right for traced separate-property contributions to community property, and the written-waiver exception (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2640.)
  Known gap: This is the actual text of Family Code section 2640(b)'s first sentence, fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and confirmed byte-identical across two fetches made with different User-Agent strings. This citation is to the same statutory section, 2640, cited by this document's companion clauses on the statute's definition (subdivision (a)) and the dollar limit on reimbursement (subdivision (b)'s second sentence, quoted separately) — they are not independent of one another; all are different parts of one enacted section. The statute's own text does not specify what particular language or form a waiver, or a writing that has "the effect of a waiver," must take beyond being written and, where not itself a waiver, signed; this document does not address that question further, nor does it address how a party establishes tracing of a contribution to a separate property source, which the statute's text does not itself define.

THE AMOUNT OF REIMBURSEMENT IS LIMITED TO THE CONTRIBUTION ITSELF
Family Code section 2640 fixes the amount of reimbursement in specific terms: the amount reimbursed shall be without interest or adjustment for change in monetary values, and may not exceed the net value of the property at the time of the division. By its own text, the statute reimburses only the dollar amount of the traced contribution itself, capped at the community property's net value at the time of division — it does not provide for interest on that amount, and it does not adjust the reimbursed amount upward or downward to reflect how the property's value has changed since the contribution was made.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The amount reimbursed shall be without interest or adjustment for change in monetary values and may not exceed the net value of the property at the time of the division."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2640(b) (California Legislative Information text), the statutory limit: reimbursement without interest or adjustment for change in monetary values, capped at the property's net value at the time of division (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2640.)
  Known gap: This is the actual text of Family Code section 2640(b)'s second sentence, fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and confirmed byte-identical across two fetches made with different User-Agent strings. This citation is to the same statutory section, 2640, cited by this document's companion clauses on the statute's definition (subdivision (a)) and the reimbursement right and waiver exception (subdivision (b)'s first sentence) — they are not independent of one another; all are different parts of one enacted section. This same without-interest, no-adjustment, net-value-cap sentence also appears verbatim in subdivision (c), addressed in this document's companion clause on contributions to the other spouse's separate property; it is quoted here from subdivision (b) because that is the subdivision governing contributions to community property. This document does not compare this fixed-dollar reimbursement formula to any pro-rata appreciation-sharing formula used in a different doctrinal context, and takes no position on how any such other formula works; it states only what section 2640's own text provides. The statute's text states that reimbursement occurs "in the division of the community estate" but does not itself spell out a sequential mechanics (for example, a required order of operations before other division steps); this document does not characterize the mechanism beyond that statutory phrase.

A RELATED BUT DISTINCT RULE: CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE OTHER SPOUSE'S SEPARATE PROPERTY
The same statutory section that creates the reimbursement right described in this document's other clauses also addresses a related but distinct situation: a party's separate property contributions to the acquisition of property of the OTHER spouse's separate property estate, made during the marriage. Family Code section 2640 provides that a party shall be reimbursed for such contributions unless there has been a transmutation in writing under the statute governing transmutations, or a written waiver of the right to reimbursement. This document's other clauses concern contributions to the ACQUISITION OF COMMUNITY property; this clause is included only to mark that boundary, so that a contribution to the other spouse's separate estate is not conflated with the community-property reimbursement right this document otherwise describes.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "A party shall be reimbursed for the party’s separate property contributions to the acquisition of property of the other spouse’s separate property estate during the marriage, unless there has been a transmutation in writing pursuant to Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 850) of Part 2 of Division 4, or a written waiver of the right to reimbursement."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2640(c) (California Legislative Information text), the distinct rule for a party's separate-property contributions to the acquisition of the other spouse's separate property (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2640.)
  Known gap: This is the actual text of Family Code section 2640(c), fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and confirmed byte-identical across two fetches made with different User-Agent strings. This citation is to the same statutory section, 2640, cited by this document's other authority clauses (subdivisions (a) and (b)) — they are not independent of one another; all are different subdivisions of one enacted section. This document does not address the separate transmutation-in-writing rules that subdivision (c) cross-references (Family Code section 850 and following), which govern a different question — whether property has changed character between separate and community — and are outside this document's scope.

SIGNATURE AND ACKNOWLEDGMENT — NOT A COURT FILING

Executed on September 1, 2026 at Oakland, California.
